findings.title: Dubai's GDRFA sweeps the Gulf Customer Experience Awards 2026 with six accolades
findings.summary: The General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA) Dubai, the same border authority whose post-summer "border hospitality" push was covered in the 28 August dossier, won six awards at the Gulf Customer Experience Awards 2026 (GCXA 26): four Golds ("Customer at the Heart of Everything", "Best Digital CX", "Best Use of Customer Insight and Feedback", "Best Innovation in CX"), a Silver ("Best CX Strategy"), and the event's overall "Highest Number of Awards" recognition. The source article does not state the ceremony's exact date or venue. For MECSC members, this is a useful data point on where Gulf public-sector CX investment is concentrating: a government service-delivery agency, not a bank or telecom, took the top overall honour at a regional CX awards programme, reinforcing the "border hospitality" theme already being tracked as a live GDRFA priority.

findings.title: DEWA's AI cuts customer refund processing from four days to eight minutes
findings.summary: Dubai Electricity and Water Authority has automated security-deposit refunds (up to AED 4,000) with AI, cutting turnaround from four business days to roughly eight minutes, a 99% reduction, as part of its stated ambition to be "the world's first AI-powered utility." The move sits alongside DEWA's long-running virtual assistant Rammas, which has handled more than 13 million customer enquiries since 2017 and has recently been upgraded with generative AI. The practical read for MECSC members: this is backend process automation rather than a customer-facing chatbot launch, and it's a useful reminder that "AI in CX" wins for utilities and government services increasingly show up as invisible speed improvements (refunds, approvals, verifications) rather than new conversational interfaces.

findings.title: LEAP 2026 opens today in Riyadh, betting the Gulf's AI story has moved past big numbers
findings.summary: LEAP 2026, Saudi Arabia's flagship technology and AI conference, now in its fifth edition, opens today in Riyadh and runs through 3 September, rescheduled from its original April slot due to regional disruption. Organisers expect roughly 200,000 visitors, 1,800 exhibitors, 600 startups and 1,900 investors; the prior edition (LEAP25) announced $14.9bn in AI investment on opening day alone, against a cumulative $42.4bn committed since 2022. Confirmed CX/enterprise-relevant exhibitors already pre-announced include Liferay (AI Hub for governed, data-grounded AI agents, covered 28 Aug), NTT DATA and Mannai IT. A Wamda analysis published 24 August argues the more useful signal this year isn't the headline investment total but whether commitments convert into working products: the piece frames this as watching for "integration schedules, costs and ownership" conversations rather than demos, Arabic-first products built for Arabic speakers (not merely localised Western tools) as a marker of genuine regional tech creation, and how many people in the region ship software for the first time this year. For MECSC members tracking vendor pitches this week, that's a useful filter for separating substance from investment-figure headlines.

findings.title: Bawabat Al Sharq Mall (Sharjah) runs a "Big Dreams Take Flight" back-to-school experience
findings.summary: Bawabat Al Sharq Mall hosted a back-to-school activation from 21–30 August built around a giant hot-air-balloon installation and four interactive games ("Hop to the Top", "Adventure Chase", "Catch Your Dream", "Sky Runner"), plus a dedicated arts-and-crafts zone, layered over its everyday retail mix of 350+ brands for stationery, electronics, fashion and accessories, along with dining and a Novo Cinemas anchor.
